- Plants are mostly green but with some scattered yellowing/lighter coloration
- Some plants appear lighter green or yellowish, particularly in patches
- No severe wilting or obvious lesions visible at this scale
- Field-level distribution of symptoms

Top candidates: Green_stem_disorder, Sudden_death_syndrome, Soybean_Cyst_Nematode, Phytophthora. Let me check reference images.

Now I have enough reference comparisons to make my determination. Let me assess:

**Test image key features:**
- Wide-angle field view of soybean at mid-to-late vegetative/early reproductive stage
- Mostly green, dense canopy
- Scattered lighter/yellowish patches visible throughout the field
- Corn visible in background (US Midwest context)
- No wilting or severe dead patches

**Reference comparison summary:**
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Field view (top-right) shows a nearly identical pattern — green field with scattered yellowing/browning on lower leaves; very common Midwest disease
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Bottom-right reference shows mostly green field with scattered yellowing — similar but typically more pronounced interveinal chlorosis visible at leaf level
- **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode**: Shows patches with stunted yellowing plants and visible cysts — doesn't match well at this scale
- **Green_stem_disorder**: Very late-season dead plants with green stems — doesn't match
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows more severe death patches adjacent to green rows — too dramatic
- **Phytophthora**: Wilted/dead seedlings in wet conditions — doesn't match

The field-level appearance (scattered lower-leaf yellowing in a mostly green mid-season canopy) most closely matches **Septoria_brown_spot**, which is the most prevalent early-season foliar disease in Midwest soybeans and typically begins on lower leaves, creating scattered yellow-to-brown areas visible from a distance.
